algorithm: Perform a depth-first search (DFS) to identify articulation points.
Track the discovery time of each node and the lowest discovery time of its children.
A node is an articulation point if it has at least one child in the DFS tree with a lowest discovery time equal to or greater than the discovery time of the node.
constraints: The graph is undirected and simple.
Vertices are numbered from 0 to n-1.
Edges are distinct and do not form cycles.
The function raises NetworkXNotImplemented if the graph is not undirected.
edge_cases: When the graph has no edges (n=1), the single node is an articulation point.
When the graph is a single edge (n=2), the two nodes are not articulation points.
When the graph is a single node (n=1), it is an articulation point.
parsed.inputs: n is an integer >= 1; edges is a list of distinct [u, v] pairs with 0 <= u < v < n.
parsed.output: An ascending list of articulation vertices (nodes) in the graph.
parsed.purpose: Yield the articulation points (cut vertices) of a graph.
